app_title: Didaskalos: Frequency-Based Greek Grammar Textbook Builder
subtitle: An Ancient Greek grammar textbook generated from the texts you choose — lessons ordered by what your corpus actually uses, exercises taken from it unaltered.
intro_html:
{header_image}

Didaskalos (διδάσκαλος, ‘teacher’) builds an Ancient Greek grammar textbook out of the texts you select. It reads annotated treebanks — 85 works by 25 authors and collections are built in, and you can paste your own URLs or upload XML — counts the grammatical feature of every word, and turns those counts into a syllabus. Grammar topics follow what your corpus actually uses rather than a fixed curriculum, and the exercises are authentic sentences from that corpus, each carrying its citation.

Ancient Greek pedagogy is concentrated in English and a few European languages, and for speakers of most other languages the resources are very limited or nonexistent. Didaskalos is built as a localizable solution for extending Ancient Greek language learning beyond those few. The sequencing lives in the code and the teaching language is a data file: the interface, the lesson modules, the grammatical terminology and the exported book are localized together, so adding a language needs one locale file and a translated set of modules rather than a new textbook. The translation itself is not mechanical — for a language with no Greek-teaching tradition the grammatical terminology has to be coined rather than translated. It is currently available in English and Persian, but nothing in the design is specific to either — everything language-specific lives in the lesson modules and one locale file, and the pipeline itself does not change. If you would like to translate Didaskalos into another language, I would be glad to help you through it: get in touch.

Frequency alone is a poor teacher, so the ranking is constrained in places. A fixed opening — the alphabet and an orientation to nouns, adjectives and verbs — maps the system before the counts take over; lessons that depend on each other stay adjacent, so the middle voice is always followed by deponent verbs; and frequency arranges everything after that.

There are two textbook types. Case-based explains nouns and adjectives case by case — one lesson for the accusative across every declension. Declension-based first classifies every noun and adjective into declension classes (first-declension feminine, second-declension masculine, the common third-declension stem types, and so on) and orders those lessons by how frequent each class is in your own texts.

Exercises are unaltered corpus sentences, scored by word rarity and sentence length and preferring sentences whose vocabulary earlier lessons have already introduced, so lexical difficulty climbs without any sentence being reworded. Syntactic difficulty is not scored, so the real curve is lumpy rather than gentle. Download the book as Markdown or HTML, and the syllabus and token tables as CSV; every book carries a colophon naming each source corpus, its license and its URL.

Keep in mind that the lesson modules were first drafted with the help of a retrieval pipeline over standard reference grammars and have since been hand-corrected; review is ongoing.

input_source_help: Use the repository defaults or upload files directly.
textbook_type_help: Case-based arranges noun/adjective lessons by case (one lesson for accusative, one for genitive, ...). Declension-based first classifies every noun and adjective in the treebanks into declension classes (o-stem, a-stem, etc.) and arranges the lessons by how frequent each class is in the corpus.
custom_treebank_urls_help: One URL per line or comma-separated. These are added on top of the default treebanks loaded from didaskalos/treebanks/perseus.
upload_help: Upload one or more XML files.
no_treebanks_warning: No treebanks available. Provide treebank URLs or upload XML files.
picker_hint: Choose the texts to include in the textbook.
no_lessons_warning: No lesson modules available from the default lesson set.
select_at_least_one_warning: Select at least one treebank file before building.

tb_doc_title: A Frequency-Based Textbook for Ancient Greek Grammar
tb_intro_case: This syllabus organizes grammar lessons by frequency of occurrence in the selected treebanks.
tb_intro_declension: This syllabus organizes grammar lessons by frequency of occurrence in the selected treebanks, with noun and adjective lessons grouped by declension class.
tb_setting_body: This textbook is built for **{lesson_count}** lessons, drawn from **{work_count}** work(s) — or the portions of them that the source treebanks annotate — totalling **{token_count:,}** analyzed word tokens, organized {mode}.
tb_syllabus_mode_declension: by frequency of occurrence, with nouns and adjectives grouped by declension class
tb_corpus_custom: Custom or uploaded treebank files provided at build time.
tb_corpus_desc_perseus: The Perseus Ancient Greek Dependency Treebank (AGDT), a scholarly collection of syntactically annotated Classical Greek texts maintained by the Perseus Digital Library.
tb_corpus_desc_gorman: Vanessa Gorman's Ancient Greek Dependency Trees, a large set of annotated treebanks covering the Attic orators, historians, and other prose authors.
tb_corpus_desc_harrington: J. Matthew Harrington's treebanked commentaries, published through the Perseids platform.
tb_corpus_desc_proiel-nt: The Greek New Testament from the PROIEL treebank, a morphologically and syntactically annotated edition of the New Testament in Koine Greek.

tb_coverage_lead: Cumulative coverage of these texts after this lesson:
tb_coverage_vocab_aria: The vocabulary lists so far cover {percent} per cent of the word tokens in these texts.
tb_coverage_morph_aria: The lessons so far cover {percent} per cent of the word forms in these texts.
tb_passages_intro: Continuous passages from the texts you selected, in the divisions their own editors marked. They are ordered so that the ones built almost entirely from words this book has taught come first. Read each one straight through before looking anything up.
tb_exercises_unavailable: Exercises are unavailable because combined treebank data was not provided.
tb_ex_parsing_prompt: Parse each form below: name its part of speech and give all of its grammatical features.
tb_ex_sentences_prompt: In each sentence, identify the {pos_label}(s) related to this lesson, and parse each one.
tb_ex_sentences_identify_prompt: In each sentence, identify the {pos_label}(s) related to this lesson.
tb_ex_sentences_verb_prompt: Parse each marked verb in the sentences below.
tb_vocab_prompt: The most frequent words of this kind in the texts this book is built from. They are given in dictionary form, without translations: look each one up, and write down the meaning you find.
tb_vocab_lookup_hint: The module *Using a Greek Dictionary* explains how to read an entry.
tb_vocab_lookup_cell: Read the entry for {headword} in [Perseus]({perseus_url}), or in [Logeion]({logeion_url}).
tb_core_words_note: These are the most frequent function words in the texts this book draws on. They carry little meaning on their own but hold every sentence together, and you will meet them from the first page onward. Learn them now, before the lessons that describe them arrive.
idle_body: This session will close in {seconds} seconds so the server can shut down.
